name: ACME Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (s-Flame)

sources.note: PSI-23 flightProgram field is 'International Space Station (ISS)'; investigation dates 2015-02-05 to 2019-11-24.
ACME overview states the experiments ran in the Combustion Integrated Rack on the ISS.

objective.value: Advance the ability to predict the structure and dynamics, including extinction, of both soot-free and sooty spherical diffusion flames in microgravity, comparing measurements with detailed numerical simulation of transport properties and chemical kinetics (including chemiluminescence).

sources.note: PSI-23 objective: measure transient spherical diffusion flame structure (temperature, species) for H2/CH4/diluent (soot-free) and C2H4/diluent (sooty) mixtures; determine convective and radiative extinction limits; determine the onset and nature of pulsating instabilities.
ACME overview: purpose of s-Flame is to advance prediction of structure and dynamics, including extinction, of soot-free and sooty flames.

PSI-23 is basic combustion science: it tests chemical-kinetic and transport models of spherical diffusion flames (flame structure, extinction limits, instabilities), not a prevention/detection/suppression technology.
ACME overview: ACME's secondary objective is spacecraft fire prevention, but s-Flame itself is characterised as fundamental microgravity combustion research.

safety_functions.note: Classed 'fundamental'. ACME as a project states a secondary spacecraft fire-prevention objective, but the s-Flame investigation is framed as fundamental flame-structure/kinetics research.

sources.note: PSI-23 SubResearch Area is 'Flames of gaseous fuels'; approach issues gaseous fuel/inert mixtures through a porous burner.
Challenge brief, Hardware section: the six ACME experiments featured flames of gaseous fuels.
ACME overview: ACME investigates laminar gaseous non-premixed flames.
PSI-23 approach: conventional gaseous fuels hydrogen, methane and ethylene; diluents nitrogen and helium to adjust diffusivities, and carbon dioxide to influence flame radiation.
PSI-23 experimental table (data/source/psi/tables/PSI-23.csv) fuel bottles: 100% H2, H2/CH4 blends, 50%/45% CH4 and C2H4 in N2, and H2/CH4/C2H4 diluted with He.
ACME overview: fuels are hydrogen and methane for soot-free flames and ethylene for sooty flames; various inert diluents in both fuel and chamber atmosphere.

fuel_geometry.value: Porous spherical burner issuing a fuel/inert gas mixture into the CIR chamber, producing a nominally spherical, one-dimensional stabilized diffusion flame.

sources.note: PSI-23 approach: mixtures of gaseous fuels and diluents issued into an oxidizing environment through a spherical porous burner and ignited to obtain a nominally spherical, one-dimensional stabilized flame.
ACME overview: the spherical flame, only possible in microgravity, is created with a porous spherical burner; flames are ignited at non-steady conditions and driven toward extinction.
PSI-23 experimentHardware is 'Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), ACME'.
Challenge brief, Hardware section: ACME experiments used the modular ACME hardware set in the CIR.

apparatus.value: ACME modular hardware with a porous spherical burner (constant-volume ~90 L chamber insert)

sources.note: PSI-23 experimentHardware: CIR / ACME; approach uses a spherical porous burner.
ACME overview: all ACME experiments use a single modular hardware set in the CIR, a constant-volume study with a ~90 L chamber free volume.

sources.note: PSI-23 approach: synchronized measurements including spectrally resolved images, flame and burner temperatures, radiative flux, and system operating conditions (reactant flow rates, ambient temperatures, pressures and acceleration levels).

ACME overview instrument set: imaging arrays, radiometers (thermopile ~0.2-11 micron), three PMT modules for OH*/CH* chemiluminescence, CIR gas chromatograph, chamber pressure, and SAMS-II acceleration.

sensors.note: The PSI approach names the measurement classes for s-Flame; the specific instrument set (radiometers, PMTs, gas chromatograph, SAMS-II) is described for the shared ACME hardware, so it is listed at medium confidence.

relevance_notes.value: Fundamental microgravity diffusion-flame study. It quantifies soot and extinction behaviour that ACME frames as relevant to spacecraft fire prevention (material flammability, conditions for sustained combustion), and provides buoyancy-free data for validating combustion models. It does not test a specific fire-safety hardware technology.

sources.note: ACME overview: ACME's secondary objective is spacecraft fire prevention (materials flammability, extinction behaviour); soot in microgravity flames is five to eight times that in normal gravity.
Challenge brief frames flammability limits and combustion understanding as prevention inputs for crewed habitats.

relevance_notes.note: My own synthesis (inferred), comparing the PSI/ACME objective against the brief's fire-safety framing.

value: improved combustion engine and device performance (power, efficiency, reliability)
improved computational combustion models and combustor design

sources.note: PSI-23 research impacts: diffusion-flame understanding improves performance in power, efficiency, pollutant emissions and reliability; microgravity gives high-fidelity data and simplified flow fields.
ACME overview: primary goal is to improve efficiency and reduce pollutant emission in practical terrestrial combustion and to improve computational models.
